To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) a regionalized relationship between EI and rainfall amount is obtained; b) a regionalized equation for the kinetic energy of an erosive event is obtained; c) a regionalized relation for estimating the single storm EI from the storm amount and maximum 1-min intensity is obtained; d) a rule for grouping daily rainfall data to reproduce the amount for an erosive event, is proposed and tested.

the following equations are valid for estimating the EI in the Mediterranean region: EI=1.54A; EI=2.3A0.6I30; EI=1.3A0I30, where A is storm amount, I30 is maximum 30-min rainfall intensity, and 0 is the kinetic energy.

a regionalized relationship between single storm erosion index (EI) and storm amount is proposed for the Mediterranean area, with a potential relationship of the form EI = 0.0025 A1.54, and the relationship between EI, kinetic energy and storm amount and intensity is proposed, with a potential form EI = 1.1 K1.5 I0.8.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simplified methodology for estimating the single storm erosion index in Mediterranean area.
the development of simplified methods to determine the EI index for erosive events.
the development of a simple and rapid method for estimating the single event erosion index from daily rainfall records.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed relationships for estimating the single-event kinetic energy, EI, and the grouping rule for daily rainfall data are reliable tools to estimate the single-event erosion index for erosive rainfall events in the Mediterranean area.
the proposed simplified methods can be used to estimate the rainfall factor R with a good degree of confidence, especially when a long-term daily rainfall record is not available.
the single-storm erosive potential in the Mediterranean area can be estimated by using only the rainfall amount and maximum 15-min intensity of an erosive event.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the Mediterranean area, the estimation of the rainfall factor R for the USLE can be obtained with a good accuracy by using only the amount of erosive events and the maximum 30-min intensities of the storms.
the single-storm Erosion Index (EI) in the Mediterranean area can be easily and reliably estimated using a regionalized relationship with storm amount and a grouping rule for daily rainfall data.
a simple and reliable procedure is developed for estimating the rainfall factor R in the USLE for the Mediterranean area, which requires only the knowledge of the daily rainfall amount.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EI index can be estimated from only storm amount and storm maximum intensity, without the need of the tedious computation of the kinetic energy.
the single-storm E index can be estimated with a good degree of confidence by using the amount of erosive event only.
, in order to obtain accurate results, it is essential to use data collected in the area under consideration and to take into account all the main factors that may affect the rainfall erosivity.
